thread:
maria: Quick heads up — ran the initial holdout QA for Venom-v2 (int8) on the support-query cohort and seeing a recall@10 regression vs Venom-v1 baseline, ~6% absolute on short queries. posting quick notes and outputs below. :thinking:
jin: What was the exact holdout split and quant config?
maria: 10k holdout from prod support logs (tagged cohorts: billing, auth, kb-search). quant: per-channel int8, symmetric, clamp=127, no residuals. eval command: `python eval_recall.py --model venom-v2-int8 --holdout holdout_2026_02.json --k 10 --norm l2`
ethan: Any change in the cosine similarity distribution? silhouette or cluster metrics?
maria: Yes — mean cosine between positives dropped ~0.02. KMeans silhouette on 50 clusters: baseline 0.42 -> venom-v2 0.31. UMAP projection looks more fragmented (hub-and-spoke).
sara: Can you break recall by query length? short vs medium vs long?
maria: Pasted quick breakdown:
```
recall@10 (baseline venom-v1): short<=20tok: 0.78, medium 20-60: 0.82, long>60: 0.85
recall@10 (venom-v2 int8): short: 0.72, medium: 0.79, long: 0.84
```
short queries disproportionately impacted.
nick: Interesting — short queries often rely on surface lexical signals, maybe quantization is perturbing small-norm token directions. Did you try renormalizing embeddings before indexing?
maria: Ran a quick `--norm none` vs `--norm l2` check. With no renorm the short-query gap shrank a bit (0.72 -> 0.74) but overall distribution was noisier. Still below baseline.
jin: Did you run a per-channel calibration (scale/zero) pass? we had a calibration script for int8 per-channel affine.
maria: Not yet for this run. I can replay with per-channel affine + bias (script `calibrate_int8.py --dataset holdout_2026_02.json --per_channel true`).
eval-bot: scheduled eval job 6154321010 for `venom-v2-int8-calib` (ETA 10m).
ethan: Also try whitening / PCA fit on a holdout subset then apply to both baseline and int8. we've seen whitening reduce cluster fragmentation.
sara: Could be embedding length collapse on short inputs. Can you post mean L2 norms per length bucket?
maria: mean L2 norms:
```
baseline: short 5.2, med 6.1, long 6.4
venom-v2-int8: short 4.1, med 5.9, long 6.2
```
shorts clearly lower.
nick: That points to scale shift on short inputs. Two immediate experiments: 1) per-input renorm (rescale to baseline mean by bucket), 2) per-channel affine calibration.
jin: I'll spin a run with per-channel affine + apply float-rescale for short inputs. also try int8 but with clamp=127 -> clamp=1023 (if using 16->8 pipeline?) — not sure if that's applicable here but worth checking quant params.
sara: For triage, also run neighbor-rerank test: take top-100 by brute-force and compute recall@1/5/10 after applying a small re-ranking MLP on concatenated (query, topk) pairs. if ranking recovers, it's a precision shift not recall capacity.
maria: Good idea. I'll kick off the per-channel calib run first (eval job scheduled), then do renorm and whitening experiments. Will attach UMAP and KMeans plots when ready.
eval-bot: job 6154321010 completed: `venom-v2-int8-calib` recall@10 improved short: 0.74 -> 0.76 (still -2 pct vs baseline). full metrics at /evals/6154321010/summary.json
ethan: Progress — calibration helped but not full recovery. next: pca-whitening + per-channel calibration + index rebuild with cosine.
sara: Can we also try a hybrid index (HNSW on PQ-coded vectors) to see if indexing losses amplify quantization effects? add that to the matrix.
maria: Adding steps to checklist: 1) whiten + per-channel calibrate (maria) 2) renorm by length bucket (maria) 3) hybrid index test (sara) 4) neighbor-rerank triage (nick) 5) assess CPU vs GPU inference diff (jin).
nick: I'll prepare a short reproducible script to reproduce the short-query norm collapse and share.
maria: Thanks — will update thread with plots and exact eval links. :eyes:
jin: ping me when plots are up, will run a small ablation on clamp/zero point.
maria: ack, leaving the results dir here for now: /evals/6154321000/venom-v2-int8-initial-smoke (will populate).
ethan: Nice triage, keeping this thread for followups. :thumbsup:
